title: English Practice Quiz 0959
description: A ten-question English practice quiz covering grammar, vocabulary and practical communication.

questions.question: Which sentence uses correct subject-verb agreement with 'neither'?
options: Neither of the answers is correct.
Neither of the answers are correct.
Neither answers is correct.
Neither of answer are correct.
questions.explanation: Neither is singular in standard formal usage in this construction.

questions.question: Choose the correct inversion: 'Rarely ___ such a beautiful view.'
options: have I seen
I have seen
I saw have
seen I have
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials such as rarely trigger subject-auxiliary inversion at the beginning.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'If he had left earlier, he ___ the train.'
options: would have caught
will catch
would catch
had caught
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional describing an unreal past situation.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported speech: She said, 'I have finished.'
options: She said that she had finished.
She said that I have finished.
She says that she finished yesterday.
She said she has finish.
questions.explanation: In standard backshifted reported speech, present perfect becomes past perfect.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the uncountable noun 'information'?
options: The information is useful.
The informations are useful.
An information is useful.
The information are useful.
questions.explanation: Information is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'The person to ___ I spoke was helpful.'
options: whom
which
whose
where
questions.explanation: Whom is used as the object of the preposition 'to' in formal English.

questions.question: Choose the correct phrase.
options: Despite the rain, the event continued.
Despite of the rain, the event continued.
Although the rain, the event continued.
In spite the rain, the event continued.
questions.explanation: Despite is followed directly by a noun phrase, without 'of'.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
options: The quality of the products is excellent.
The quality of the products are excellent.
The products quality are excellent.
The quality of products have excellent.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'quality', which is singular.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence to express a present wish.
options: I wish I knew the answer.
I wish I know the answer yesterday.
I wish I had know the answer.
I wish I knowing the answer.
questions.explanation: Wish + past simple expresses a present situation that is different from reality.

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct parallel structure.
options: She enjoys reading, writing and cycling.
She enjoys reading, to write and cycling.
She enjoys to read, writing and cycle.
She enjoys read, write and cycling.
questions.explanation: Parallel items in a series should use matching grammatical forms.
